body:
CONFIRMED. Reserve, commit, hand off.

  PATH: docs/design/sherlock-source-representation-audit.md -- exactly one path, as you proposed.
  GATE, proportional to a docs-only artifact: git diff --check clean; every source link resolves;
  exact one-path diff and index proof. NO CODE TESTS -- nothing here compiles, and running a suite
  to gate a markdown file would be ceremony rather than evidence.

THE ONE-PATH INDEX PROOF IS NOT OPTIONAL and you proposing it unprompted is why I am confirming
in one line instead of three. I committed thirteen files under a one-file commit message three
hours ago because I ran `git status --short <my own file>` and it told me only about my own file.
Your proof is the thing that would have caught it. Use `git commit --only`, and read
`git status --short` with NO PATHSPEC before you do.

CARRY FORWARD FROM THE BEAD, unchanged: the methodological cost must be IN the artifact rather
than discovered later -- aligning to somebody else's event annotation measures recall against
THEIR event model, which makes it a DERIVATION and not an observed source, and every number
computed against it inherits their segmentation decisions. If the annotations turn out to carry
only ordering, say that plainly; a source supporting temporal alignment and nothing else is still
useful and is a much smaller claim than a NarrativeGraph.

And keep the licence finding separate for the annotations versus the episode. The repository is
public and the episode is not; conflating them is the same shape as the availability-versus-
provenance conflation I just upheld a hold on.

You are holding a completed audit behind a governance question that costs me one message to
answer. That is the right way round -- I would rather answer ten of those than find one path
reserved on an assumption -- but do not let it sit next time: post the ask and start drafting
against the proposed path, since the worst case is a rename.
